title: Tenant hedged slice allocator with KV-retention fairness
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Goal: design and implement a hedged slice allocator for the continuous batching runtime that enforces tenant SLOs while balancing KV-cache retention across tenants, reducing noisy-neighbor eviction churn, and optimizing GPU memory usage. The allocator should: 1) allocate per-tenant time-slices (slices) to the continuous batcher using hedged allocation (soft extra quota for lagging tenants), 2) drive KV cache retention by a tenancy-aware retention score instead of LRU only, 3) support non-disruptive soft-suspension of low-priority slices under severe memory pressure, and 4) expose observability and rollback controls in the Console for canary rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler respects tenant latency SLOs >= 95th percentile targets across representative workloads
KV retention score reduces repeated hot-set evictions by >= 30% on synthetic contention tests
GPU memory high-water events reduced or made less frequent in mixed workloads compared to baseline
Rollout config (canary percent, circuit-breaker) available in console and defaults validated in staging
Automated unit/integration tests cover hedged allocation heuristics and forced preemption scenarios
design_notes: We will move away from strict time-slice ceilings to a hedged model: each tenant has a target slice budget computed from SLA tier, recent latency trend, and recent token spend. When a tenant is lagging on latency (predictive window), allocator grants a hedged boost up to 20% of budget for a short window. To avoid KV thrash, each slice is assigned a KV-retention-score that combines recency, frequency, and 'stickiness' (tenant-specified long-lived contexts). Retention-score decays with a configurable half-life (default 60s) so transient spikes don't permanently chase eviction. Under memory pressure, the allocator prefers soft-suspension (holdback) of hedged slices before hard eviction of owned KV segments. Rationale: soft-suspend preserves performance for tenants with strict SLOs while reducing full-KV flush churn. Trade-offs: hedging can increase short-term GPU utilization and per-token cost; mitigation via conservative defaults and auto-tune based on production telemetry.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike) - 1 week: prototype hedged allocator logic in runtime simulation harness, validate on replay traces (trace set: serve-mix-2025-q4)
Phase 2 - 2 weeks: integrate allocator in batcher, implement KV-retention-score and decay, add metrics (slice-granted, hedged-boost, kv-eviction-reason)
Phase 3 - 1 week: implement soft-suspend mechanism and graceful resume path; add unit/integration tests for eviction/resume
Phase 4 - 1 week: internal canary in staging with 5% traffic, monitor console dashboards, iteratively adjust decay/boost parameters
Phase 5 - rollout & docs: run 25% canary, then progressive ramp with circuit-breaker; publish design doc + console controls
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Hedged boosts increase overall token latency variance. Mitigation: cap boosts, add backpressure signal to upstream SDKs, experiment with shorter boost windows.
Risk: Retention-score complexity may regress tail-latency if mis-weighted. Mitigation: expose weights as runtime flags and auto-tune using reinforcement-like policy in staging.
Risk: Soft-suspend followed by hot resumption could create bursty load. Mitigation: stagger resume windows and use randomized jitter per-tenant.
Risk: Unexpected interaction with dedicated capacity autoscaler. Mitigation: test with dedicated pools in staging and add coordination shim with autoscaler (follow-up ticket).
metrics: KV eviction rate (evictions/sec) bucketed by reason (memory-pressure|policy|LRU)
GPU memory high-water events per hour
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator decision tree, synthetic replay harness with mixed workloads (chat + long-context generation + embeddings), chaos test that forces KV pressure and verifies soft-suspend/resume semantics, staging canary with traffic shadowing and A/B comparison to baseline scheduler.
rollout_and_monitoring: Start with 5% internal canary (staging) -> 25% customer-internal Beta -> 100% gradual rollout. Monitor Console dashboards: hedged_alloc_ratio, kv_eviction_reduction, tenant_95p_latency_delta. Circuit-breaker: if any tenant 95P latency worsens >10% for 10m, automatically disable hedging for that tenant and trigger alert to oncall.
open_questions: What is the long-term policy for tenant-specified stickiness? allow labels/TTL on KV entries or only inferred?
Should hedged boosts be billable differently? coordinate with pricing/product team
How to surface per-tenant retention hints in Console without leaking cross-tenant usage patterns?
